leading_positions.synthesis: Three members put the magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene ballot first, each with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. They share the argument that the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the 2018 correlated and superconducting states form a separable theory-plus-experiment pair, and that the twist angle is a new control parameter spawning a wider moire field. Olsson opened with only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero and moved to all three after discussion. They differ in emphasis (Eriksson on theory-led prediction and timeliness, Mehlig on the statistical-physics idea of tunable interaction versus bandwidth, Olsson on interface registry) and in how far they accept that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled; all three want a citation built on the flat-band prediction and observed phases rather than a mechanism. B021 is also named as an alternative by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce, so it is the most widely acceptable second choice, but the committee has not stated that it is anyone's first choice beyond these three.

Danielsson and Pearce (the chair, who is reporting his own position here) prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, with a citation on the prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and time-reversal-invariant topological insulators. They share the points that the interpretation has been stable for more than fifteen years and that Mele should not be replaced. Eriksson and Mehlig list B030 as an alternative, Mehlig preferring Hasan in place of Mele in his opening, and Johansson ranked it third in the opening but does not carry it into round 1. Lindroth and Olsson say they would not oppose it if the credit can be settled. Nobody disputes its scientific standing; the open questions are the missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, Hasan's 3D work, and overlap with the 2016 topology prize.

Kroll and Lindroth prefer Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks reaching about 10^-18, citing the magic-wavelength idea, independent confirmation in several countries, concrete uses in geodesy and constants tests, and the cleanest two-name credit on the shortlist. They differ in their alternatives (Kroll B021 and B006; Lindroth B006 and B021) and both concede that precision-spectroscopy prizes in 2005 and 2012 raise a novelty question and that groups at NIST, PTB, RIKEN and elsewhere are passed over. Mehlig and Olsson name B024 as an alternative, and several other members call the case strong but weigh it below a new-field discovery.

Johansson alone prefers Cirac, Zoller and Blatt for trapped-ion quantum computation and simulation, arguing it is distinct from the 2012 prize because the subject is gate-based computation and simulation and that it has thirty years of independent confirmation. Kroll and Lindroth list B006 as an alternative, and Johansson's first opening choice, circuit QED (B002), is now only an alternative because of the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize and a disclosed proximity to that field. Others (Danielsson, Olsson, Kroll) say the 2012 overlap, and the shared Cirac and Zoller names with B020, need a sharper argument.

areas_of_agreement: Every member preferred a single-part prize in round 1, and no member argued that any of B021, B030, B024 or B006 lacks scientific merit; disagreements are about ordering, maturity and credit.
B021, B030 and B024 are each described by members outside their supporter group as serious or deserving candidates, and B021 appears in the alternatives of five of the eight members.

Several members agree that B030's citation should be worded so as not to imply all of topological insulator physics, and that B021's citation should rest on the flat-band prediction and observed phases rather than on the superconducting mechanism.

Members who comment on B002 (Danielsson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson) regard it as premature or awkward after the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits and the four-name credit; B033 is regarded as a major discovery whose credit is hard to resolve, with Danielsson listing it only as an alternative.
Danielsson and Pearce, the two B030 supporters, defend Mele as inseparable from Kane on the original proposal.
scientific_disputes: Whether the unsettled microscopic origin of superconductivity and correlated phases in twisted bilayer graphene is acceptable for recognition (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson say a platform and phenomenology prize is enough; Kroll, Pearce, Danielsson and Lindroth say the interpretation is less settled than for topological insulators or clocks).
Whether breadth of follow-on activity in B021 counts as merit or partly reflects open questions (Mehlig and Eriksson versus Kroll and Lindroth).

Whether optical lattice clocks are a new invention or an increment on the lines honoured in 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (control of single quantum systems); Kroll and Lindroth argue the former, Mehlig, Olsson and Eriksson weigh conceptual novelty above precision.
Whether trapped-ion computation is distinct from the 2012 prize on measurement and control of single quantum systems (Johansson says yes; Olsson and Danielsson want a sharper argument).

Whether a measurement-capability prize (B024) or a new-state-of-matter prize (B021 or B030) should take priority this year; Mehlig and Eriksson mention B024 only as a possible second part of a shared prize, but no member proposed a multi-part configuration.
attribution_disputes: B030: whether the three names should be Kane, Mele and Molenkamp (Danielsson, Pearce), or Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan (Mehlig's opening), and how the omitted Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal that guided the HgTe experiment and Hasan's 3D work should be handled in the citation.

B021: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, and the independent groups of Dean, Young, Yazdani and Efetov are outside the credit; earlier moire band-structure work by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto is also outside it. Olsson opened with two names and now proposes three, so the two-versus-three question is settled in the files but may recur.
B024: the two-name credit is called clean by Kroll, Lindroth and others, but both supporters note Ludlow, Lemonde, Takamoto and the NIST, PTB and RIKEN groups who carried the 10^-18 milestone.
B006: whether Blatt is the right experimental laureate given Monroe and Wineland-lineage contributions; Cirac and Zoller also appear on B020, which complicates any later optical-lattice award.

B033: Danielsson is the only member who lists it as an alternative; Lindroth and Pearce say three founding-leader names are a proxy for two collaborations of thousands, so the credit may not identify decisive contributors.
maturity_disputes: B021: about eight years since the 2018 experiments is short beside B030 (stable for fifteen years) and B024 (a decade or more of replication); Kroll, Pearce and Lindroth raise it, and Mehlig concedes it, whereas Eriksson and Olsson argue the phenomenology is reproduced by many laboratories and recognition is timely.

B030: whether the 2016 prize for topological phases and phase transitions makes a second topological prize too close in time; Danielsson and Pearce say the 2016 prize did not cover time-reversal-invariant insulators, while Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson treat overlap as a real concern.
B002: the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits makes timing awkward for a circuit QED award.
B024: the headline payoff, such as a redefinition of the second or a new-physics limit, has not yet arrived; Kroll lists this as a question for the committee.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers, WACQT) disclosed that B002 circuit QED is close to his own field and collaborators, discounts his opening first choice, and recommends taking no decisive role on B002; he reports no specific conflict for B006, B021 or B030.

Kroll disclosed time in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his doctoral period and a neighbouring laser-spectroscopy background, relevant to B024 although he reports no documented tie to Katori or Ye; he asks the committee to note this.

Eriksson disclosed professional proximity to B019 through his own use of density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory, listing B019 only as an alternative and reporting no personal tie to its credited names.
Olsson noted her Japanese university exchanges could be checked against B005 and B024 but reports no specific conflict.
Lindroth flagged a possible bias towards atomic-physics topics as a theoretical atomic physicist, without a specific conflict.

Danielsson, Mehlig and Pearce report no specific conflict; the chair's documented connections (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+, XL-Calibur, KTH) involve no credited name, and the chair notes he supports B030 and has no expertise in the condensed-matter and quantum-optics fields that dominate the shortlist.
questions_for_round2: For B021, is a citation built on the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states acceptable to B030, B024 and B006 supporters despite the unresolved mechanism, and what would those members need to see to accept the timing?

For B030, can the committee defend Kane, Mele and Molenkamp against Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan, and what citation wording credits the proposal and first observation without implying all of topological insulator physics?

Does the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions make B030 too close, given that Danielsson and Pearce regard the time-reversal-invariant insulator as a distinct discovery while five members raise overlap?

Kroll asks why the chair ranked B024 sixth: is the weight on proximity to the 2005 and 2012 prizes or on the narrow sense of discovery, and how do B024 supporters distinguish the lattice clock from those prizes?

Should the committee prefer a new-state-of-matter achievement (B021, B030) or a measurement achievement (B024) this year, and would any member support a two-part prize combining them given the three-laureate limit?
For B006, what is the sharper argument that gate-based trapped-ion computation is distinct from the 2012 prize, and does the shared Cirac and Zoller credit with B020 constrain either ballot?
Does any member wish to move B033, B002, B019 or B005 into a preferred configuration, and if so how is the attribution or timing objection raised by Pearce, Johansson, Lindroth and Eriksson answered?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 has three first-choice clusters (B021 with three members, B030 with two, B024 with two) and one singleton (B006). Most alternatives point to B021, but no member has yet ranked a cluster above its own with a stated willingness to move. The central tradeoff is between B021's cleaner theory-plus-experiment attribution and B030 and B024's longer confirmation record, and members have raised a few objections to each that the second round can test. The chair supports B030 and records that this summary counts only what is explicit in the eight round-1 files.
